title: Oven Temperature Sensor Open
shortDescription: The oven temperature sensor (RTD) is reading open circuit.
fullDescription:
Haier ovens use a PT500 or PT1000 RTD at the rear of the cavity. E1 appears when resistance is infinite, usually from a broken sensor or disconnected plug.

A new RTD typically reads around 1080 ohm at room temperature (PT1000). Replace and reconnect to clear the fault.

fixSteps.title: Unplug
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect oven from power.

fixSteps.title: Access sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove rear panel or back-wall sensor retainer.

fixSteps.title: Test and replace
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance; replace sensor if infinite.

whenToCallPro: If wiring needs tracing behind the cavity.

faq.q: Can I keep using the oven?
faq.a: No - without a sensor the control cannot safely regulate heat.

title: Oven Temperature Sensor Shorted
shortDescription: The oven temperature sensor reads near zero ohms.
fullDescription:
E2 is the shorted-sensor counterpart to E1. A crushed lead or internal failure drops the resistance to near zero, telling the control the oven is extremely hot and preventing heating.

Replace the sensor and inspect the harness route for pinching or heat damage.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Fit a new RTD and inspect wiring.

whenToCallPro: If the short is in foam-embedded wiring.

faq.q: Do I need the OEM part?
faq.a: Match RTD type (PT500 vs PT1000) and connector exactly.

title: Over-temperature Trip
shortDescription: The oven exceeded its maximum safe temperature.
fullDescription:
E3 is raised if the RTD reads above the manufacturer's over-temperature limit (often 300 °C outside self-clean). A stuck relay, failed control, or misbehaving element can cause it.

Turn off the breaker and let the oven cool; if E3 returns on the next cycle, call service as the relay board may be welded on.

fixSteps.title: Breaker off
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect immediately if oven overheated.

fixSteps.title: Service
fixSteps.instruction: Have relay board and control inspected.

whenToCallPro: Always - runaway heat is a fire hazard.

faq.a: No - do not operate the oven until the fault is cleared.

title: Door Lock Motor Failure
shortDescription: The self-clean door lock mechanism has not reached its commanded position.
fullDescription:
E4 appears when the lock motor is driven to lock or unlock and the limit switch does not confirm within the timeout. A seized motor, broken cam, or failed switch cause E4.

If the door is stuck locked, do not force it; a lock motor assembly swap is needed.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn breaker off for 5 minutes to reset.

fixSteps.title: Replace lock
fixSteps.instruction: Swap the lock motor assembly on top of the oven cavity.

whenToCallPro: If the door is locked with hot contents inside.

faq.a: Cancel from the control; if the door stays locked after cooldown, E4 is posted.

title: Door Switch Fault
shortDescription: The oven door switch reports an impossible state.
fullDescription:
E5 is posted when the door switch reads closed while the lock is commanded open, or vice versa. A failed switch or loose harness are the usual causes.

Test continuity at the switch; replacement is inexpensive and straightforward.
symptoms: Interior light always on or off

fixSteps.title: Test switch
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug, remove the switch, test for continuity change when actuated.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Fit a new switch if it fails the test.

faq.q: Can I run bake with E5?
faq.a: No, the oven will refuse to start for safety.

title: Cooling Fan Fault
shortDescription: The oven cooling fan is not running at the tacho-expected speed.
fullDescription:
Haier ovens have a tangential cooling fan that keeps the control compartment cool. E6 is raised if its tacho is absent or too slow.

A dusty fan cage, worn bearing, or failed motor are the typical causes.
symptoms: No fan noise or loud fan

fixSteps.title: Clean fan
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum fan inlet and impeller.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Fit a new cooling fan motor if the bearing is rough.

whenToCallPro: If fan is fine but E6 still posts.

faq.q: Will the oven run without the fan?
faq.a: No, for safety the oven disables heating.

title: Meat Probe Fault
shortDescription: The internal meat probe reads out of valid range.
fullDescription:
When a probe is used, E7 means the probe reads open, shorted, or impossibly high. A new probe or a clean probe-jack contact usually fixes the issue.

If you are not using a probe, remove it from the jack to clear the code.

fixSteps.title: Remove probe
fixSteps.instruction: Pull probe and clean the jack with a dry cotton swab.

fixSteps.title: Replace probe
fixSteps.instruction: Fit a new OEM meat probe if errors continue.

whenToCallPro: If the jack or board needs service.

faq.a: Yes, once removed the oven will clear the probe-related lockout.

title: Touch Panel Stuck Key
shortDescription: A touch key is reading pressed continuously.
fullDescription:
E8 is posted when a capacitive key stays active longer than allowed. Cleaning fluid, food splatter, or a cracked glass face are the usual culprits.

Power cycle after cleaning; if the fault returns, replace the control panel.

causes.cause: Liquid or debris on touch area

fixSteps.title: Clean
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe touch surface with a dry microfibre cloth.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Breaker off for 2 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Replace panel
fixSteps.instruction: Swap touch control panel if fault persists.

videoSearchQuery: Haier oven E8 touch key stuck

faq.a: Excess water on the panel can be pushed into the sensor area - let it dry fully.

title: Communication Error
shortDescription: Touch panel and main control cannot communicate.
fullDescription:
E9 appears when the serial link between the touch control board and the main relay/power board is lost. A loose ribbon after service or a failed board are the usual causes.

Power cycle and reseat the harness first.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Breaker off for 5 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Reseat ribbon
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug, remove rear cover, reseat the ribbon.

whenToCallPro: If reseating does not clear it and board replacement is required.

faq.q: Can I keep using the oven?
faq.a: No - the control cannot safely modulate heat without communication.

title: EEPROM / Configuration Fault
shortDescription: The oven control cannot read stored configuration.
fullDescription:
E10 signals that the EEPROM on the control board is corrupted or missing model configuration. The oven will not operate.

A service-mode reload sometimes works; otherwise the control board must be replaced with one preloaded for the model.

fixSteps.title: Service reload
fixSteps.instruction: Technician enters service mode and loads model profile.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: Swap main board if reload fails.

faq.a: User resets do not restore EEPROM configuration.
